content.title: MP Materials Stock Surges, Then Dips. Wall Street Can’t Catch Up.
content.summary: MP Materials  stock whipsawed investors on Tuesday, eventually closing at another record.  Recent gains haven’t given Wall Street a chance to catch up to increasing bullish sentiment on rare-earth players.  Both USA Rare Earth and Ramaco stocks have posted double-digit percentage gains in recent days.

content.title: Trump’s Takeover Of Canadian Rare Earths Miners Raises Major Concerns
content.summary: Washington doubles down on critical minerals, with the Trump administration buying stakes in companies like Trilogy Metals, MP Materials, and Lithium Americas.

content.title: Why Nothing Can Stop MP Materials Stock, at Least for Now
content.summary: MP Materials  stock and shares of other rare-earth miners jumped again on Monday, extending last week’s rally after China tightened export controls on the minerals.  MP Materials stock rose 21.3% to $95.06, a record close.  Smaller rare-earth companies  USA Rare Earth  and  Ramaco Resources  rose 18.6% and 11.1%, respectively, after closing higher on Friday.

content.title: Rare earth stocks surge, Broadcom pops on OpenAI deal
content.description:
Here are some of the stories Wall Street is watching on Monday, Oct. 13. OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) and Broadcom (AVGO) announced an agreement for data center chips. Rare earth stocks are surging on continued tensions between the US and China. Jefferies Financial (JEF) is seeking to reassure investors following the bankruptcy of auto-parts supplier First Brands.

Stay up to date on the latest market action, minute-by-minute, with Yahoo Finance's Market Minute.

content.title: China Moves to Limit Rare Earth Exports. These Mining Stocks Are Gaining.
content.summary: China is at it again, attempting to roil commodities markets it dominates.  Shares of rare earth miner  MP Materials  and other commodity producers were rising Thursday after China made additional moves to restrict exports of rare earth materials and lithium-ion batteries.  MP Materials stock traded as high as $78.32 before sliding back to $72.29, closing up 2.4% on Thursday, while the  and  lost 0.3% and 0.5%, respectively.
